_comment: Tier-2 for fourc::shell#4, and a FALSIFICATION of its recipe. The entry told the reader to 'output both N and M tensors via STRESS_STRAIN'. STRESS_STRAIN is not a SHELL7P element key — appending it to the element line is rejected with "After parsing, the line still contains 'STRESS_STRAIN plane_stress'." from core/io/src/4C_io_input_spec.cpp (it belongs to WALL and MEMBRANE). The key that does exist is the boolean IO/RUNTIME VTK OUTPUT/STRUCTURE.STRESS_STRAIN together with IO's STRUCT_STRESS / STRUCT_STRAIN enums, and what it writes is element_cauchy_stresses_xyz, nodal_cauchy_stresses_xyz, element_GL_strains_xyz and nodal_GL_strains_xyz — Cauchy stress and Green-Lagrange strain tensors in the global frame. The .vtu contains no membrane-force and no bending-moment resultant field at all (both counts 0); the only shell-specific extra is OPTIONAL_QUANTITY, here shell7p_thickness_director. Resultants have to be integrated in post-processing. Verified by execution 2026-08-06 against 4C 2026.2.0-dev at /home/alexander/4C/build/4C.
expect_in_output: After parsing, the line still contains 'STRESS_STRAIN plane_stress'.

_mutation.note: remove the pathology: stop putting the WALL/MEMBRANE key on the shell element line. The leftover-token diagnostic vanishes and EXIT_ELEMENT_KEY becomes 0, so the fixture must go red.
remove the output request: run the second arm without the IO block. No .vtu with stress fields is written, so the field-name assertions cannot be met and the fixture must go red.
